quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results: CEO John Ketchum: adjusted EPS increased 9.7% year over year, and 9.5% through the first nine months. CFO Mike Dunne: FPL EPS rose $0.06 on regulatory capital employed growth of approximately 9.2%; FPL capital expenditures were approximately $2.4 billion in the quarter and full-year FPL capital investments are expected at approximately $12 billion; FPL's regulatory ROE for the 12 months ending September 2026 will be approximately 11.8%; FPL reversed approximately $172 million of the rate stabilization mechanism, leaving an after-tax balance of roughly $1.5 billion; FPL retail sales rose 2.8% (1.4% weather-normalized, on customer growth). Energy Resources adjusted earnings grew approximately 13% (adjusted EPS +$0.06): new investments, which now include federal hubs, +$0.09 (power generation portfolio growth and initial contributions from federal hubs); existing assets +$0.05 (wind resource approximately 101% of the long-term average vs 90% a year earlier); customer supply -$0.04 (timing of origination); other -$0.04 (interest expense, capital recycling timing). Corporate and other -$0.01.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 adjusted EPS +9.7%; Energy Resources adjusted earnings +13%; FPL regulatory capital employed +9.2%; FPL 2026 capital investments approximately $12 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (CFO Mike Dunne, CEO John Ketchum): 2026 adjusted EPS expectations of $3.92-$4.02 unchanged and NextEra is targeting the high end, which the CEO says already includes expected El Nino impacts on wind in Q4 (generation expected at 90%-95% of the long-term average); adjusted EPS CAGR of 8%+ through 2032 and targeted 8%+ from 2032 through 2035 off the 2025 base of $3.71, with average annual operating cash flow growth at or above that range from 2025 to 2032; in combination with Dominion Energy the CEO expects 9%+. Dividends per share expected to grow roughly 10% per year through 2026 and 6% per year from year-end 2026 through 2028. A 50 basis point move in rates has only a $0.01-$0.03 per share impact in 2028. CFO: transmission rate base expected to grow at roughly 20%-25% CAGR from 2025 through 2032, with possible upside in gas transmission; Energy Resources President and CEO Brian Bolster: hitting the targets would mean on the order of a $50 billion utility within Energy Resources. FPL's typical residential bill is projected to increase 2% annually on average through the end of the decade.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 adjusted EPS $3.92-$4.02 (targeting high end); 8%+ adjusted EPS CAGR through 2032; transmission 20%-25% CAGR

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog and recontracting (CEO John Ketchum, CFO Mike Dunne): Energy Resources added 3.7 GW of renewables and storage to its backlog in the quarter, including 2.4 GW of battery storage, the fourth consecutive quarter above 3.5 GW; the backlog now totals nearly 36.7 GW after more than 1.8 GW of new projects were placed into service since the last call; approximately 15 GW was added in the last 12 months, more than two-thirds of the midpoint of 2026-2029 development expectations is achieved and 17.6 GW is left to add to reach that midpoint. Recontracting: a 20-year PPA for approximately 1 GW of the Point Beach nuclear plant in Wisconsin (subject to Public Service Commission of Wisconsin approval), putting the plant's full output under contract into the 2050s; over 250 MW of renewables recontracted since the last call, nearly 1,400 MW year to date at roughly a $20 per megawatt hour premium above recent realized pricing, and nearly 2,400 MW in total this year. Transmission: regulated and invested capital plus secured capex across electric and gas transmission rose roughly 25% to approximately $12.7 billion since December 2025; the gas transmission business formed a joint venture with Chesapeake Utilities Corporation to build a $1.2 billion, 97-mile intrastate gas pipeline in South Florida.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog nearly 36.7 GW (+3.7 GW in Q3, 2.4 GW storage); recontracted nearly 2,400 MW YTD; transmission capital approximately $12.7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: FPL large load (CEO John Ketchum, FPL President and CEO Scott Bores): FPL's large load tariff, whose protections are largely codified into Florida law, means 'hyperscalers know exactly how we plan to serve them in Florida'; FPL raised large load expectations from 6 GW to 8 GW by 2032 and remains confident it will announce a large load transaction by the end of the year. Bores: FPL has a pipeline of over 20 GW of interest; these are 'multi-billion dollar deals that take some time' and FPL is building consensus with local communities before announcing; to serve the first couple of gigawatts of large load FPL mainly needs to build battery storage, given its base load gas and nuclear fleet. CFO Mike Dunne declined to size the first deal.
quarterly_data.figure: FPL large load expectations 8 GW by 2032 (from 6 GW); over 20 GW of interest

quarterly_data.signal: Energy Resources large load and federal hubs (CEO John Ketchum): more than 20 GW of large load projects advanced, over 18 GW of them gas-fired generation. Definitive agreements signed to develop, construct and operate three federal hub projects across Texas and Pennsylvania totaling approximately 16.5 GW, which secured $5.7 billion in initial funding year to date; Energy Resources earns fees on a predetermined schedule for development and construction and for the first 20 years of operation, without investing capital, and expects about 50% of the adjusted EPS it would earn by owning the projects; construction and PPA solicitation run in parallel, with significant load served as early as 2028 and 2029 using behind-the-meter generation and a ramp to the campuses' full requirements from 2030 through 2032. The three hubs equal roughly the top end of the 4-8 GW natural gas development expectations on an adjusted EPS basis; building and owning battery storage at the hubs could add 6-11 GW, an approximate 15%-30% upside to storage expectations. CEO: payments in 2026 and 2027 will be relatively modest, growing through 2032, with operating fees from 2032-2052 roughly half the EPS of ownership. At the Department of Energy's Paducah site in Kentucky NextEra expects to build and own up to 2 GW of natural gas and up to 2.6 GW of battery storage for a data center campus; the hub pipeline is 30 potential hubs, expected to rise to 40 by year end.
quarterly_data.figure: federal hubs approximately 16.5 GW, $5.7 billion initial funding; storage upside 6-11 GW; Paducah up to 2 GW gas and 2.6 GW storage

quarterly_data.signal: Nuclear (CEO John Ketchum, Energy Resources President and CEO Brian Bolster): the Duane Arnold nuclear plant in Iowa remains on track to be recommissioned and re-enter service no later than Q1 2029. NextEra is assessing various SMR OEMs and has 6 GW of SMR co-location opportunities at its nuclear sites plus new greenfield sites; any new nuclear build needs commercial terms with risk-sharing that limits NextEra's exposure. Bolster: NextEra has 'a bias' towards SMRs but would consider large-scale nuclear if the customer strongly prefers it and protections are right.
quarterly_data.figure: Duane Arnold back in service no later than Q1 2029; 6 GW SMR co-location opportunities

quarterly_data.signal: Hurricane Isaias and FPL operations (CEO John Ketchum): FPL assembled a restoration workforce of approximately 17,000 people from 29 states and restored power to more than 97% of affected customers by Tuesday after the storm exited early Saturday; not a single hardened transmission or distribution pole failed, underground lines performed approximately 14 times better than overhead lines, and smart grid technology avoided approximately 140,000 outages. FPL's typical residential bill is approximately 37% below the national average, non-fuel O&M is more than 70% below the industry average per megawatt hour and reliability is more than 60% better than the national average; in Northwest Florida the inflation-adjusted bill is approximately 25% lower than in 2018 before the Gulf Power acquisition.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 17,000 restoration workers; more than 97% restored by Tuesday; approximately 140,000 outages avoided

quarterly_data.signal: Pending combination with Dominion Energy (CEO John Ketchum): shareholders of both companies approved it on September 3; Virginia and South Carolina hearings are set for November and December with final orders expected in January 2027, North Carolina expert witness hearings begin in February 2027, federal reviews continue, and closing is still expected in the second half of 2027. The enhanced Virginia package doubles residential bill credits from two to four years ('almost $2 billion in rate credits' before the Virginia SCC), adds $100 million of shareholder-funded bill assistance through 2038 and $100 million for workforce development, creates up to a $5 billion Virginia supplier program over five years, and commits 600 new NextEra Energy jobs in a new Richmond co-headquarters tower plus at least 400 supplier jobs under letters of intent, 1,000 in total. CEO: the combined company would become the second largest in the United States in nuclear.
quarterly_data.figure: close expected 2H 2027; almost $2 billion of Virginia rate credits; up to $5 billion Virginia supplier program; 1,000 Virginia jobs

quarterly_data.signal: Market views (CEO John Ketchum, Energy Resources President and CEO Brian Bolster, CFO Mike Dunne): CEO: 'power demand is expected to increase sixfold across this country', so permitting reform for linear infrastructure (electric and gas transmission) matters; demand for solar remains strong and NextEra sees 'a real competitive advantage' in its supply chain, with storage expansion from four to potentially eight hours adding appeal. Bolster: customers have focused on capacity, hence the pickup in storage, and he expects 'a shift in the coming quarters back towards more energy than capacity'. CFO: NextEra locks in interest rates when it signs PPAs and can pass higher rates through because customers need power and tax credits lower wind and solar costs; Bolster: 'we were never the low-cost bidder', so higher rates are flushing out low-cost bidders and should help market share and returns. CFO: NextEra intends to hold more of its $7 billion-$12 billion capital recycling plan unless a buyer values assets far more.

connects_to.relationship: Point Beach nuclear power purchase agreement with Wisconsin Electric Power Company

contracts.signal: NextEra executed a 20-year power purchase agreement for approximately 1 GW of its Point Beach nuclear plant in Wisconsin at a competitive price, subject to approval by the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin; the plant's full output is now contracted into the 2050s. CEO John Ketchum: Point Beach's current contract is with We Energies and the new contract takes effect as those contracts roll off in 2031-2033, with an overall contribution of roughly $0.21 on average; Brian Bolster: a recontracting of the existing facility for 20 years, not an upgrade.
